summary: Transparent corporate TLS proxy strips ALPN (http2) and re-signs certs causing streaming connections to downgrade and fail
description:
Issue summary:
Customer FinServCo running Private deployment in eu-central reports intermittent failures for streaming inference (server->client streaming responses via HTTP/2/gRPC). Failures started after a corporate proxy upgrade.

Impact:
- Streaming sessions either fail to establish or fall back to non-streaming HTTP/1.1 causing SDK errors and truncated responses for chat/streaming endpoints.
- Affects production traffic for a subset of users behind corporate perimeter appliances; non-proxied users are unaffected.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC peering + egress through corporate perimeter proxy appliance).
- Region: eu-central-1.
- SDK: redwood-js v2.3.1 and redwood-go v1.8.
- Proxy appliance: vendor-reported "SecureWeb 5.4" transparent TLS proxy with corporate root re-signing.

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) From an internal client behind the corporate proxy, init a streaming chat request via SDK with response_mode: "stream".
2) Observe immediate error in SDK: "streaming not available on connection" or the connection drops after a few tokens with "grpc: stream error: CODE_INTERNAL".
3) From same client bypassing the proxy (direct internet or from a bastion), streaming works normally.

Observed behavior:
- TLS negotiation between client and proxy shows ALPN negotiated as "http/1.1" (proxy->server) even though client offers "h2".
- Proxy re-signs server certs with corporate CA and strips TLS extension that advertises HTTP/2 support.
- Server logs show connection established without HTTP/2, then SDK attempts to use streaming features and fails.
- Intermittent: some requests succeed when proxy chooses passthrough or preserves ALPN; most fail after proxy upgrade.

Expected behavior:
- ALPN should include "h2" so HTTP/2 stacks are negotiated end-to-end. Transparent TLS proxies that re-sign must preserve ALPN and TLS versions compatible with HTTP/2.

Initial logs provided by customer:
- SDK client debug: "ALPN negotiated: http/1.1"
- Server side (api-gateway) connection metadata: "negotiated_protocol: http/1.1, tls_version: TLSv1.2"
- tcpdump on customer's edge: Client ClientHello contains ALPN h2, ProxyClientHello contains http/1.1 only.

Notes: Customer claims corporate security policy mandates TLS inspection, but proxy vendor suggests a configuration toggle to preserve ALPN and SNI.

2026-03-10 10:02 - Support Tier 2 (Anita R.): Requested tcpdump and TLS ClientHello/ServerHello captures; customer uploaded pcap showing ALPN mismatch.
2026-03-11 14:40 - Networking (Liam O'Connor): Reproduced with vendor appliance in lab. Confirmed proxy rewrites ALPN when re-signing with corporate CA by default.
2026-03-12 08:55 - Customer (FinServCo/N. Patel): Vendor provided a firmware note that 'preserve_alpn = false' default was introduced in v5.4; recommended setting preserve_alpn = true as workaround.
2026-03-12 11:20 - Liam O'Connor: Sent workaround and recommended config to customer; asked to validate in prod canary and report results.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Transparent TLS proxy re-signs TLS session and omits ALPN h2 from the re-negotiated ClientHello/ServerHello, causing server to only advertise HTTP/1.1 and preventing HTTP/2/gRPC streaming.
Reproduced in lab by deploying SecureWeb 5.4 with default settings: observed ALPN removed when proxy performed re-signing for inspected flows.
Server (api-gateway) accepts HTTP/1.1 and continues serving but SDKs expecting HTTP/2-level streaming fail. No server-side stack traces beyond stream errors in gRPC layer.
Packet captures: original client Hello includes ALPN h2, proxy-to-server Hello lacks h2. TLS versions are >= TLS1.2 so not a legacy-protocol fallback issue.
Workaround test: enabling 'preserve_alpn=true' on SecureWeb preserves h2 and restores streaming in lab. Customer to confirm on their prod canary group.
Risk assessment: Many corporate TLS inspection appliances and older configurations may default to removing ALPN; guidance required for private deploy customers with mandated TLS inspection.
resolution:
Provided short-term workaround: customer to set 'preserve_alpn=true' or configure TLS passthrough for *.redwood-inference.internal endpoints on their proxy/VPN appliance; support shared vendor firmware note and CLI commands. Customer reported initial canary success and is rolling to 20% of users.

Long-term / product follow-up items created:
- Add a detection warning in Private deployment health checks that flags ALPN removal/HTTP2 downgrade on control/data plane paths.
- Document a TLS inspection guidance page for Private customers explaining ALPN preservation and websocket/grpc passthrough requirements.
- Track compatibility matrix for known proxy appliances and default settings that break HTTP/2 streaming.

Status: Workaround accepted by customer; closing pending after customer confirms full production rollout.
